newsitem.title: UK: UK confident Amsterdam EU summit will end in deal.
newsitem.headline: UK confident Amsterdam EU summit will end in deal.

text.p: British officials said on Wednesday they were confident that next week's summit on the future shape of the European Union would end successfully despite major issues yet to be resolved.

The Amsterdam summit is meant to set the seal on 18 months of talks over the future of the EU but member states are still arguing over the timetable for introducing European Monetary Union (EMU) and a host of other matters.
Britain insists on retaining control over its own borders and opposes Franco-German plans to integrate the Western European Union, an informal defence alliance, into the EU.

"I think the realisation will grow that this (the summit) isn't the most revolutionary event in European history. My judgement is that there will be agreement in Amsterdam," one official told reporters.
Some matters would be decided only at the last moment, he said, adding that the Dutch hosts were due to circulate a new text for discussions on Thursday.
"I can't see the big issues being resolved before Amsterdam... I expect defence and border controls will be settled together (at the summit)," the official said.

Prospects for EMU nosedived after a row in Germany over plans to revalue gold reserves to help to meet EMU targets and by the new French socialist government's demand for more time to consider the stability pact that will underpin budgetary discipline in the new single currency zone.
"The uncertainty over EMU and the stability pact will increase the determination (to conclude a treaty)," the official said.
Britain says it is very unlikely to sign up to the first wave of EMU, which is scheduled to start in 1999.

The official dismissed speculation that the Dutch could quickly hold another summit if the first one failed, saying many ministers would have already left for the handover of Hong Kong to China at the end of June.
If the Amsterdam summit did end in deadlock, he said, ministers were most likely to meet again in Luxembourg at the end of July.
